title: Portfolio Website — Built with AI
summary: Personal portfolio site evolved from a class project into a full SPA with a blog CMS, admin tool, and 14+ project posts — the blog system and content pipeline were vibe-coded with Claude

data.text: My personal portfolio at katerina.wang started as a CSIS 1430 class project in Summer 2023 and has gone through three major rewrites over three years. The current version is a vanilla JavaScript single-page application with a Node.js backend, a JSON-based blog/CMS system, and an admin tool for writing and editing posts — all deployed on AWS Amplify. The blog system and the bulk of the project content were built through AI-assisted development ("vibe coding") with Claude, making this project a case study in how I use AI as a development partner.

items.content: 2023 — Class project origin: started as static HTML/CSS/JS pages for CSIS 1430 at SLCC, hosting course assignments like a birthday greeting page, lottery game, tic-tac-toe, and a Bootstrap pizza site — all hand-coded with no frameworks

2025 — SPA redesign (solo): rebuilt the entire site as a dynamic single-page app over winter break — replaced static HTML with JSON-driven content rendering, added a Typed.js intro animation, Swiper.js skill carousel, GLightbox media viewer, fade-in page transitions, and a fully responsive layout with custom fonts (Caveat, Gugi, Tomorrow, Ubuntu Sans)

2026 — Blog CMS with AI: vibe-coded the blog system, admin tool, Node.js API server, and content pipeline with Claude — transforming the site from a static showcase into a full content management system with 14+ detailed project posts

data.text: The August 2026 sprint was the first AI-assisted phase. Working with Claude in Cowork sessions, I went from having a static project grid to a fully functional blog platform in a single day. Here's what was built through that collaboration:

items.content: Blog system with timeline UI: a blog page with posts grouped by year and month, collapsible year sections, tag filtering via clickable chips, and a live search bar — all rendering dynamically from index.json with no page reloads

EditorJS-compatible post renderer: post.js parses a JSON content array and renders paragraph, header, list (with nested items), code, quote, delimiter, image, PDF embed, and button blocks — consecutive button blocks are automatically grouped into a centered action bar with GLightbox integration for video URLs

Node.js API server: server.js (296 lines) serving as both a static file server with SPA fallback and a REST API — /api/save writes post JSON and updates the index, /api/delete removes posts and cleans up orphaned media, /api/upload handles base64 image/file uploads with timestamped filenames, and /api/reindex triggers a full index rebuild

Orphaned media cleanup: on every post save, the server diffs old vs. new media URLs in the post's content blocks and automatically deletes files that are no longer referenced — preventing media directory bloat

Path-based SPA routing: replaced hash-based routing (#projects) with History API paths (/projects, /post/project/slug) plus a server-side fallback that serves index.html for extensionless paths — enabling clean URLs and proper browser back/forward behavior

CSS/JS modularization: refactored a monolithic style.css and script.js into per-page modules (home.js/css, blog.js/css, projects.js/css, post.js/css, experience.js/css) — keeping the main files under 200 lines each

data.text: In September 2026, I used Claude to populate the blog with detailed project posts for every course and major project in my portfolio. The workflow: I connected my local project folders, Claude read the actual source code (every Java file, every C file, every assignment), and generated EditorJS JSON posts that described each project's technical implementation at the code level — not just what the project does, but how it works and what I specifically contributed. This produced 14 detailed posts across 6 courses and standalone projects, each with accurate technical descriptions drawn directly from the source.

items.content: Source-code-driven descriptions: Claude read every file in each project — not summaries or READMEs — and produced technical write-ups referencing specific classes, methods, data structures, and algorithms actually used in the code

Duplicate detection: automatically identified when the same project appeared across two courses (a sorting comparison project shared between CSIS 2420 and CSIS 2430) and cross-linked instead of duplicating

Index rebuild on startup: added a rebuildIndex() function to server.js that scans all category subdirectories and regenerates index.json from individual post files — so posts committed directly to the filesystem (bypassing the admin tool) are picked up automatically when the server restarts

Batch file delivery: post JSON files were generated in Claude's workspace and committed directly to local project folders via the Cowork device bridge — no manual copy-paste for any of the 14 posts or index updates
Original 2023 site: all initial HTML/CSS/JS pages, responsive layouts, and class project implementations

2025 SPA architecture: the full redesign — dynamic JSON-driven rendering, Typed.js animation, Swiper.js carousel, GLightbox integration, fade-in transitions, responsive grid layout, custom font stack, and the visual identity (animated avatar with morphing CSS border)
Ongoing content and maintenance: resume updates, work experience entries, favicon, deployment configuration on AWS Amplify, and iterative layout adjustments across 30+ commits over 2023–2026

data.text: This project demonstrates my approach to AI-assisted development: I own the architecture and visual design, AI accelerates the implementation of well-scoped systems (a blog CMS, a content pipeline) and handles bulk content generation where accuracy matters more than personal voice. The AI-generated code follows the patterns I'd already established — vanilla JS, no build tools, JSON data files, modular CSS — rather than introducing its own stack. Every commit is reviewed and pushed by me, and the AI contributions are attributed in commit messages.

items.content: Frontend: vanilla JS SPA — no framework, no build step. index.html loads per-page modules (home.js, blog.js, projects.js, post.js, experience.js) and a shared script.js router using the History API. Content is fetched from JSON and rendered as DOM fragments via <template> elements

Backend: 296-line Node.js HTTP server with no dependencies beyond stdlib — serves static files, provides CRUD API routes for posts, handles media uploads with base64 decoding, and rebuilds the post index from the filesystem on startup

Data model: posts are individual JSON files in portfolio/posts/{category}/{slug}.json using EditorJS block format, with a derived index.json for listing and search. No database — the filesystem is the source of truth
Libraries: Typed.js (intro animation), Swiper.js (skill carousel), GLightbox (image/video lightbox), Font Awesome (icons) — all loaded from CDN, no npm build pipeline for the frontend
Deployment: AWS Amplify with custom domain (katerina.wang), auto-deploy from GitHub
